_source: ADR Chapter 3.3 — special provisions. PART 4 — numbers 397–650.

provisions.397: Mixtures of nitrogen and oxygen with 19.5–23.5% oxygen by volume (no other oxidizing gases) — Class 5.1 label not required.
provisions.398: Entry covering mixtures of butylenes, 1-butylene, cis-2-butylene, trans-2-butylene; isobutylene → UN 1055.
provisions.400: Sodium ion cells and batteries (including when installed in equipment) are exempted from ADR provided: they are fully short-circuited (verifiably), 2.2.9.1.7.2(a,b,d,e,f) are met, marking is applied per 5.2.1.9, a 1.2 m drop test is passed (except when installed in equipment), they are protected against damage, and the goods are carried only per 3.4 and within the column 7a limit.
provisions.401: Sodium ion cells and batteries with organic electrolyte → UN 3551/3552; with aqueous alkaline electrolyte → UN 2795; with metallic sodium/sodium alloy → UN 3292.
provisions.402: The material must have a vapour pressure ≤1.1 MPa at 70°C and a density ≥0.525 kg/l at 50°C.
provisions.403: Nitrocellulose membrane filters (≤53 g/m², ≤300 g net per inner packaging) are exempted from ADR provided paper interleaving (≥80 g/m²) is used and specified packing configurations apply (rolls/sheets/discs with suitable protection).
provisions.404: Vehicles powered by sodium ion batteries (carrying no other dangerous goods) are exempted from ADR if the battery is fully short-circuited (verifiably).
provisions.406: Material in pressure receptacles ≤1000 ml may be carried under the LQ provisions (3.4); receptacles per P200, with pressure × volume product ≤15.2 MPa·l; must not be packed together with other dangerous goods.
provisions.407-408: Fire-extinguisher discharge devices (pyrotechnic substance, no other dangerous goods) — must meet the criteria of division 1.4S per Test Series 6(c); must be protected against accidental activation; may be assigned to Class 9 (UN 3559) under additional conditions (exemption 2.2.1.1.8.2, safe extinguishing agent, external temperature ≤200°C after activation, competent authority approval); does not apply to safety devices covered by special provision 280. Separately: entry applies only to aqueous TMAH solutions (+≤1% other components), with classification exceptions for Packing Group I/II at specified concentrations.
provisions.409-499: (Reserved, except for the entries listed separately)
provisions.502: UN 2006 (nitrocellulose-based self-heating plastics) and UN 2002 (celluloid, scrap) — Class 4.2.
provisions.504: UN 1847/1849/2949 (hydrated sulfides/sodium hydrosulfide, minimum 25–30% water) — Class 8.
provisions.506: Pyrophoric alkaline earth metals — Class 4.2; UN 1869 magnesium/magnesium alloy (>50% Mg, granules/turnings/ribbons) — Class 4.1.
provisions.507: UN 3048 aluminium phosphide pesticide with inhibitor additives — Class 6.1.
provisions.508: UN 1871 titanium hydride, UN 1437 zirconium hydride — Class 4.1; UN 2870 aluminium borohydride — Class 4.2.
provisions.510-511: UN 1755 chromic acid solution — Class 8. UN 1625/1627 mercury nitrates, UN 2727 thallium nitrate — Class 6.1; solid thorium nitrate, uranyl nitrate (solution or solid) — Class 7.
provisions.512-513: UN 1730/1731/1732/1733 (antimony chlorides/fluoride) — Class 8. UN 0224 barium azide, dry or wetted with <50% water — Class 1; UN 1571 barium azide, wetted with ≥50% water — Class 4.1; UN 1854 pyrophoric barium alloys — Class 4.2; UN 1445/1446/1447/1448/1449/2719/2741/3405/3406 (barium salts) — Class 5.1; UN 1565/1884 (barium cyanide/oxide) — Class 6.1.
provisions.515: UN 1581/1582 chloropicrin mixed with methyl chloride — Class 2.
provisions.516-517: UN 1912 methyl chloride and dichloromethane — Class 2. UN 1690/1812/2505/2674/2856/3415/3422 (fluorides) — Class 6.1.
provisions.518-521: UN 1463 chromium trioxide, anhydrous — Class 5.1. UN 1048 hydrogen bromide, anhydrous, gaseous — Class 2. UN 1050 hydrogen chloride, anhydrous, gaseous — Class 2. Solid chlorites and hypochlorites — Class 5.1.
provisions.522: UN 1873 perchloric acid, 50–72% — Class 5.1; concentrations >72%, or mixtures with a liquid other than water, are forbidden for carriage.
provisions.523: UN 1382/1385 anhydrous sulfides (and hydrates with <30% water), UN 2318 sodium hydrosulfide with <25% water — Class 4.2.
provisions.524: UN 2858 zirconium articles ≥18 µm thick — Class 4.1.
provisions.525: Solutions of inorganic cyanides: >30% cyanide ion → PG I; >3–30% → PG II; >0.3–3% → PG III.
provisions.528: UN 1353 fibres/fabric impregnated with weakly nitrated nitrocellulose, not self-heating — Class 4.1.
provisions.529: UN 0135 mercury fulminate, wetted with ≥20% water or alcohol-water mixture — Class 1; mercurous chloride/calomel — Class 6.1 (UN 2025).
provisions.531: Mixtures with a flash point <23°C containing >55% nitrocellulose (any nitrogen content) or ≤55% with nitrogen content >12.6% — Class 1 (UN 0340/0342) or Class 4.1 (UN 2555/2556/2557).
provisions.533: UN 1198 formaldehyde solution, flammable — Class 3; non-flammable solutions containing <25% formaldehyde are not subject to ADR.
provisions.534: Motor spirit with a vapour pressure at 50°C up to 150 kPa is still treated as material with vapour pressure ≤110 kPa.
provisions.536-539: Solid naphthalene → UN 1334. UN 2869 titanium trichloride mixture, non-pyrophoric — Class 8. Solid sulfur → UN 1350. Isocyanates in solution, flash point >23°C — Class 6.1.
provisions.540: UN 1326/1352/1358 (hafnium/titanium/zirconium powder, wetted with ≥25% water) — Class 4.1.
provisions.541: Nitrocellulose mixtures with water/alcohol/plasticizer content below the required level — Class 1.
provisions.542: Entry covers talc containing tremolite or actinolite.
provisions.545: UN 0401 dipicryl sulfide, wetted with <10% water — Class 1.
provisions.546: UN 2009 zirconium, dry (sheets/strips <18 µm) — Class 4.2; ≥254 µm not subject to ADR.
provisions.548-549: Chlorosilanes reacting with water to give a flammable gas — Class 4.3; flash point <23°C, no gas evolution with water — Class 3; flash point ≥23°C, no gas evolution — Class 8.
provisions.550-551: UN 1333 cerium (plates/bars/rods) — Class 4.1. Isocyanate solutions, flash point <23°C — Class 3.
provisions.552: Powdered pyrophoric metals/alloys — Class 4.2; those reacting with water to give a flammable gas — Class 4.3.
provisions.553: Mixtures of hydrogen peroxide and peracetic acid: test criteria (no detonation/deflagration, SADT ≥60°C for a 50 kg package) determine whether the mixture is not classified under those criteria, or falls under Class 5.2.
provisions.554: Metal hydrides reacting with water to give a flammable gas — Class 4.3; UN 2870 aluminium borohydride (including installed in equipment) — Class 4.2.
provisions.555: Metal dusts/powders not liable to spontaneous ignition, non-toxic, but reacting with water — Class 4.3.
provisions.558: Pyrophoric metals/alloys — Class 4.2; metals/alloys not reacting with water, not pyrophoric, not self-heating, but flammable — Class 4.1.
provisions.560: Elevated temperature liquid material, N.O.S., ≥100°C, below its flash point — Class 9 (UN 3257).
provisions.561-562: Chloroformates predominantly corrosive — Class 8. Pyrophoric organometallic compounds — Class 4.2; those reacting with water and flammable — Class 4.3.
provisions.563-564: UN 1905 selenic acid — Class 8. UN 2443/2444/2475 (vanadium compounds) — Class 8.
provisions.565: Waste not otherwise specified from biological treatment/research, with minimal probability of Class 6.2 infectious content; decontaminated waste is not subject to the Class 6.2 provisions.
provisions.568: Barium azide with less than the required water content — Class 1, UN 0224.
provisions.581: Mixtures of propadiene with methylacetylene: a table of percentage compositions defines the permitted technical names "Mixture P1"/"Mixture P2".
provisions.582-583: Refrigerant gas mixtures designated "R...", with a table of vapour pressure/density, give technical names F1/F2/F3 etc.; certain refrigerants (R11, R113, R113a, R133, R133b) are not themselves Class 2 but may be components of the F1-F3 mixtures; a further table of mixtures A/A01/A02/A0/A1/B/B1/B2/C gives permitted technical/trade names (Butane, Propane — only as supplementary names for tanks).
provisions.584: The gas is not subject to ADR if: it makes up ≤0.5% of the gas phase, is contained in undamaged, sealed metal capsules of ≤25 g gas content and ≤0.75 g/cm³ capacity.
provisions.586: Powdered/wetted hafnium, titanium, zirconium — a visible excess of water is required; with sufficiently large particle size (≥53 µm mechanically produced / ≥840 µm chemically produced) they are not subject to ADR.
provisions.587-591: Barium stearate/titanate — not subject to ADR. Hydrated aluminium bromide/chloride (solid) — not subject to ADR. Ferric chloride hexahydrate — not subject to ADR. Lead sulfate with ≤3% free acid — not subject to the Class 8 provisions.
provisions.592: Empty, uncleaned packagings/tanks/containers that have held this material — not subject to ADR.
provisions.593: Gas used to refrigerate unclassified goods (medical/biological samples) in double-walled receptacles per P203(6) — not subject to ADR except for 5.5.3.
provisions.594: UN 1044 fire extinguishers protected against accidental discharge and UN 3164 articles, pressurized (pneumatic/hydraulic) fitted with pressure relief — not subject to ADR provided packing/construction meets the requirements of the manufacturing or user country.
provisions.596-598: Cadmium pigments (sulfides, selenosulfides, cadmium salts) — not subject to ADR. Acetic acid solutions ≤10% — not subject to ADR. New or used batteries meeting fixing/securing conditions and protected against short circuit and leakage — not subject to ADR ("used" means for recycling after use).
provisions.600: Vanadium pentoxide, fused and solidified — not subject to ADR.
provisions.601: Finished pharmaceutical products (medicines) for retail sale/personal use — not subject to ADR.
provisions.602-603: Phosphorus sulfides containing yellow or white phosphorus — forbidden for carriage. Hydrogen cyanide not meeting the requirements of UN 1051/1614 — forbidden for carriage; considered stable when <3% water and pH 2.5±0.5, clear and colourless.
provisions.607: Mixtures of potassium nitrate and sodium nitrite with an ammonium salt — forbidden for carriage.
provisions.609: Tetranitromethane containing combustible impurities — forbidden for carriage.
provisions.610-611: Material containing >45% hydrogen cyanide — forbidden for carriage. Ammonium nitrate containing >0.2% combustible material other than Class 1 substances — forbidden for carriage.
provisions.613-614: Chloric acid solution >10%, and mixtures with a liquid other than water — forbidden for carriage. TCDD at concentrations classed as highly toxic per 2.2.61.1 — forbidden for carriage.
provisions.616-618: Material containing >40% liquid nitrate esters requires a positive result of the exudation test (2.3.1). Except where the type of explosive already indicates it, the trade name must appear on the package. Oxygen concentration in the vapour space of receptacles containing 1,2-butadiene must be ≤50 ml/m³.
provisions.623: UN 1829 sulfur trioxide must be stabilized; at a purity ≥99.95% it may be carried without inhibitor in tanks provided the temperature is kept ≥32.5°C, with a corresponding entry in the transport document.
provisions.625: Packages must be clearly marked "UN 1950 AEROSOLS".
provisions.632-633: Material regarded as spontaneously flammable (pyrophoric). Packages/small containers holding this material must be marked "Keep away from sources of ignition" in the official language of the country of origin (plus English/French/German if that language is different).
provisions.635: Packages containing these devices need not bear label model No. 9, unless the devices are fully enclosed and cannot be identified.
provisions.636: Lithium or sodium ion cells and batteries of low mass/capacity (≤500 g, ≤20 Wh, ≤100 Wh, ≤1 g/2 g lithium) collected for sorting, disposal or recycling are exempted from ADR (including from special provision 376) subject to: packing per P909, a quality assurance programme (limit of 333 kg per transport unit), and marking "LITHIUM/SODIUM ION BATTERIES FOR DISPOSAL/RECYCLING".
provisions.637: Micro-organisms/genetically modified organisms (dangerous only to something other than humans/animals) are not subject to ADR once approved by the competent authorities; carriage of live vertebrates/invertebrates is forbidden unless there is no alternative; temperature-control information must be given for perishable materials.
provisions.638-640: Materials treated as similar to self-reactive substances (see 2.2.41.1.19). See 2.2.2.3, classification code 2F, UN 1965. Materials in the same packing group may have different ADR tank codes (owing to differing properties) — for tanks, the transport document must be supplemented with "Special provision 640X" (X = the letter shown in column 6), which may be omitted when the tank meets the strictest applicable requirements.
provisions.642: This entry (from the UN Model Regulations) applies only to fertilizer ammoniating solutions containing free ammonia per 1.1.4.2; otherwise UN 2073/2672/3318 apply.
provisions.643-644: Mixtures of bituminous material with aggregate/gravel do not meet the Class 9 criteria. (Provision 644 deleted.)
provisions.645: The classification code shown in column 3b may be used only with the written approval of the competent authority (a classification approval certificate bearing a reference number); verification by Test Series 6 may be required.
provisions.646-647: Carbon activated by steam activation — not subject to ADR. Vinegar/food-grade acetic acid ≤25% acid — subject only to simplified requirements (corrosion-resistant packaging material, annual inspection, filling without spillage, tight closures, combination packagings permitted per P001).
provisions.648: Articles impregnated with pesticide (fibreboard, paper rolls, cotton bales, films) in hermetically sealed packagings — not subject to ADR.
provisions.650: Waste consisting of packaging residues, solidified residues and liquid residues of paint may be carried as UN 1263, PG II, or as UN 3082, with additional packing options (P002/IBC06, flexible plastics IBCs 13H3-5, testing at PG II level) and bulk carriage (closed vehicles/containers, UN 1263 and UN 3082 may be co-loaded and declared together as UN 1263); the transport document must read, e.g., "UN 1263 WASTE PAINT, 3, II, (D/E)".
